Subject: Follow-up: how KV-cache affects billing for long conversations

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering team about how billing works for our use case: long-running support conversations where we keep rehydrating persona state from a KV cache. Two quick questions: 1) When a cached prefix is rehydrated (we pull a 3k-token persona state from KV and then send a 512-token follow-up prompt), do you bill for the full 3.5k tokens or only the 512 new tokens? 2) Do you round per-request (e.g., round up to nearest 8/16/64 token increment) or is there a monthly aggregation?

I've attached our POC requirements. We're trying to compare unit economics across vendors and want to understand the edge-case here before finalizing the POC budget.

Hi Maria — great questions. Short answer: we try to avoid double-billing for cached context, but there are a couple of nuances I want our pricing and infra teams to confirm. Looping in Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (engineer) to provide an authoritative breakdown and a sample cost calc for your POC.

High-level notes to set expectations: 
- We bill primarily on token I/O (input + output).
- For KV-rehydrated prefixes we *normally* do not charge for tokens that are only looked up and not re-sent over the wire — but if we reconstruct the full prompt for the model we may amortize the reconstruction cost.
- We have a minimum per-request billing quantum (we typically use a 16-token minimum for hosted API requests) and rounding rules that can change for Dedicated/Reserved customers.

Marissa / Karthik: please see Maria's attached POC requirements and advise on exact math and any available discounts for RDW-5521 (ACME POC).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-devs.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: how KV-cache affects billing for long conversations

Thanks for the invite, Hannah. Maria — quick practical breakdown and the current standard policy (we can offer exceptions on committed Dedicated deals):

1) KV-cache vs billed tokens
- If we serve a continuation that only references cached KV entries (we pull keys server-side and don't re-send all cached tokens as part of the prompt to the model), we charge for: (a) the output tokens generated; (b) a small per-request cache lookup surcharge that we bill as equivalent to a 16-token minimum.
- If the model execution requires fully reconstructing the prompt (i.e., we rehydrate and concatenate a cached 3k-token prefix + 512-token prompt and actually send 3.5k tokens into the model), we bill input+output tokens for that call. In practice we recommend avoiding full rehydration where possible.

2) Minimums & rounding
- Hosted API: per-request rounding up to the nearest 16-token quantum. Example: 1 token generated => billed as 16 tokens. 33 tokens => billed as 48 tokens.
- Dedicated/Reserved: rounding to nearest 8-token quantum, and we can configure per-route batching to reduce overhead.
- Monthly aggregation? We do not aggregate across requests for quantum rounding; rounding is per-request. However, for significant monthly commits we apply a post-hoc smoothing credit to approximate per-token usage (effectively reversing rounding on net usage).

3) Discounts & packaging for RDW-5521
- For a 12-month reserved POC commit > $45k/month, we can reduce the per-request minimum to 8 tokens and waive the cache lookup surcharge for up to 1M cache lookups/month.
- If you want the cheapest possible economics for heavy KV rehydratation patterns, Dedicated with per-route caching controls is the right fit.

Attaching a small pricing matrix with the two sample scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and illustrative math. I'll produce a sample quote if you confirm expected average prompt length and concurrency.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: how KV-cache affects billing for long conversations

Adding an engineering perspective and an example to make the policy concrete. Two operational modes we see:

A) Server-side KV lookup (preferred):
- Sequence: model receives a short prompt + pointers to KV entries. Runtime pulls entries, performs a compact representation and only injects a small summary token sequence (e.g., 64 tokens) into the model. Billing: billed_input = prompt_tokens + added_summary_tokens; billed_output = generated_tokens. Cache-lookup surcharge applies (we currently treat this as 16-token equivalent on Hosted).

B) Full prompt reconstruction (what you described):
- Sequence: we rehydrate a 3,000-token persona + 512-token prompt and send full 3,512 tokens to the model. Billing: billed_input = 3,512 + billed_output. No cache lookup surcharge because it's just normal token billing.

Concrete math example (Hosted API):
- Scenario 1 (server-side lookup + 200 token reply): prompt 512 tokens, summary injected 64 tokens, model generates 200 tokens. Billing = (512+64+200) => 776 tokens, rounded up to nearest 16 => 784 tokens billed.
- Scenario 2 (rehydration full + 200 token reply): prompt 3,512 tokens + 200 = 3,712 tokens billed, rounded up => 3,712 (already multiple of 16).

Operational note: our runtime will attempt to compress cached context into summaries automatically when you enable "aggressive prefix compaction" for a route. That reduces raw token billing but may occasionally affect output fidelity; we can control the compression aggressiveness per-route.

Happy to run a quick script against your sample traces to show expected monthly spend under both modes.

—Karthik
Sr. SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Maria — thanks for the patience and great detail in the doc. To summarize and propose next steps: 

Summary:
- We will not double-bill cached tokens when we can serve continuations via server-side lookups; instead you see output tokens + a lookup surcharge (hosted = 16-token min).
- If the runtime reconstructs & sends the full cached prefix to the model, we bill the full input+output tokens for that call.
- Hosted rounding is per-request to nearest 16 tokens; Dedicated can go down to 8-token quantum with a commit.

Proposal:
1) If ACME confirms expected average prompt length (we saw ~512 in your doc) and expected average response size (approx 150–250 tokens), we'll run a 30-day simulated usage run against your traces and provide a modeled monthly bill for both Hosted and Dedicated modes.
2) For RDW-5521 we can issue a draft quote with the following optional concession: reduce hosted lookup surcharge to 8-token-equivalent for the first 1M lookups if you sign a 3-month POC with a $25k/month minimum.

Can you confirm concurrency (avg requests/sec) and whether you prefer Hosted POC (faster) or Dedicated POC (better long-run unit cost)? Once you confirm I'll push a formal quote and a DocuSign link.

Best — Hannah
